Fixes #342489

Backport of #342490 to `release/1.143`. Cherry-picked with `-x` from `e013f3efb4341e19b146714bf44b543a2436e231` without conflicts.

## Summary

Use the existing custom-option button builder for modified-file confirmations when protocol options are present. This preserves option IDs and approval/denial kinds instead of returning the displayed `Allow` label.

For sandbox writes, the preserved `save-sandbox-path` selection allows the existing client flow to save the offered path to user sandbox settings and grant the pending SDK request. The host's sandbox validation is unchanged. Confirmations without custom options retain their existing label-based behavior.

## Regression coverage

- Allow and Skip preserve their protocol IDs and kinds with a file-edit preview, both inline and in the confirmation carousel.
- Keyboard acceptance matches the displayed custom primary action.
- Existing legacy modified-file confirmation coverage remains in place.

## Validation

The release base was the same source commit used by the original fix. `git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}' 'e013f3efb4341e19b146714bf44b543a2436e231^{tree}'` confirmed identical source trees (`29bf338152426bdc832bcd8b4158bafbff9fdd50`), so the original validation below is reused; builds and tests were not rerun in the isolated backport worktree. `git diff --check origin/release/1.143...HEAD` passed on the backport.

Passed:

- `npm install` — completed successfully.
- `npm run build-fast` (existing Build Fast task) — completed successfully.
- Default `VS Code - Build` task (Ctrl+Shift+B), restarted through `Restart VS Code - Build` — core transpilation and core typecheck completed with zero errors; extension compilation completed; Copilot bundling and typecheck completed with zero errors. Watchers remain running.
- `npm run eslint -- src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\browser\widget\chatContentParts\toolInvocationParts\chatModifiedFilesConfirmationSubPart.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\widget\chatListRenderer.test.ts` — passed for both files.
- `git diff --check` — passed before committing.
- Editor diagnostics — no errors in either changed file.

Test execution remains unverified due to runner/environment failures:

- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\widget\chatListRenderer.test.ts --grep 'sandbox path file confirmation|Accept matches the displayed primary action' --reporter dot` — Electron exited with code `-2147483645` before executing tests.
- `npm run test-browser -- --browser chromium --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\widget\chatListRenderer.test.ts --grep 'sandbox path file confirmation|Accept matches the displayed primary action' --reporter dot` — failed before executing tests because Chromium navigation to the local test server returned `ERR_NETWORK_ACCESS_DENIED`.

The pre-fix failure was correlated in renderer and agent-host logs. A live post-fix agent write has not been exercised.

## Manual verification

1. With agent sandboxing enabled, ask the agent to create a text file outside the configured writable paths.
2. In the file-preview confirmation, choose Allow to add the offered path to user sandbox settings and retry.
3. Verify that the read/write setting is saved and the tool proceeds inside the sandbox without a host-policy rejection.
4. Verify Skip denies the request without saving access, and keyboard acceptance behaves like clicking Allow.
5. Repeat with the confirmation carousel enabled and disabled; verify ordinary file confirmations without custom options still work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render a modified-file confirmation with protocol custom options, inline or in the confirmation carousel
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The pending tool invocation synchronously constructs the confirmation subpart, groups the supplied options, creates at most one approve and one deny button plus dropdown actions for additional options, and mounts the widget before the confirmation is usable.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work is O(k) in the custom-option count and unchanged O(f) in the modified-file count; the realistic sandbox request has k=2, and the diff does not change file-list rendering.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each visible confirmation renders independently on the UI thread. Carousel deferral may create a transcript and carousel representation through existing behavior, but the diff adds no queue, task, or asynchronous fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates in button construction. Cold and warm renders do the same bounded option grouping; no cache key, miss retry, or negative-cache behavior is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the changed branch performs only linear in-memory grouping and bounded DOM/button allocation during render.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Protocol custom-option cardinality is not statically capped, but modified-file sandbox confirmations are evidenced with two options; no realistic large-cardinality trigger is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Compared with the prior single legacy button built from tool-specific labels, the diff creates the protocol-defined approve/deny controls, but for realistic option counts the additional synchronous UI work is constant-sized and necessary for the intended interaction.

Scenarios.Scenario: Accept the custom primary action to save a sandbox path and continue the pending tool
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The click synchronously records the selected option, then confirmation handling awaits one USER_LOCAL configuration update before dispatching one ChatToolCallConfirmed action; the pending tool cannot continue until both complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the offered sandbox path to USER_LOCAL configuration via configurationService.updateValue
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one write for one accepted save-sandbox-path confirmation; concurrent grants are serialized rather than burst.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The modified-file button returned the displayed label instead of the option ID, so this existing save branch was not reached for this UI path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The confirmation flow awaits the write before notifying the agent host, so it is on the tool-resume critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch ChatToolCallConfirmed with the selected option ID to resolve the pending agent-host tool call
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One dispatch per confirmed tool invocation, protected by existing one-shot confirmation state/guards.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same confirmation dispatch occurred, but without resolving the protocol option or saving the sandbox path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The tool resumes only after this action is dispatched; the diff changes its metadata, not its cardinality.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One explicit save operation and one dispatch per accepted sandbox-path confirmation. Existing user path arrays are copied/deduplicated linearly in their configured path count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Concurrent sandbox setting writes are globally serialized by the existing Sequencer; confirmation dispatch remains one-shot per invocation through existing guards.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The configuration service supplies the current user-local value; there is no result cache or retry cache. Warm state does not remove the required persistence write, and queued expired requests are skipped by the existing currentness check.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the click callback, awaitConfirmation path, saveSandboxPathGrant implementation, Sequencer, and single dispatch path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Configuration persistence latency depends on the platform and settings backend, but cardinality is fixed at one user-requested write and there is no added fan-out.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The newly reachable settings write is the explicit behavior selected by the user, is serialized and bounded to one write, and does not add repeated or concurrent boundary work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Choose the custom deny/Skip action on a modified-file confirmation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The click records the deny option and the existing confirmation handler sends a single denial action; no sandbox settings persistence occurs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch one denied ChatToolCallConfirmed action with selectedOptionId
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One action for the selected confirmation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Confirmation resolution already dispatched one action; the diff makes the protocol deny option selectable in the modified-file UI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The action resolves/cancels the pending tool call and is the only expensive boundary on this path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One dispatch per denied pending tool invocation, independent of modified-file or option counts after the click.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each invocation resolves once; no new concurrency, batching change, or fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is used or affected.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the custom button callback and existing confirmation dispatch logic.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the path is one-shot and bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff exposes the intended deny action without increasing dispatch cardinality or adding persistence work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. The production change adds O(k) option grouping and small DOM allocation for custom modified-file confirmation buttons. The only newly reachable expensive boundary is one serialized user-settings write after explicit sandbox-path approval; existing confirmation IPC remains one-shot. No actionable performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.
